title: Treatment-by-time interaction with missing visits: random-intercept model and ML likelihood-ratio test
source_relation: adapted: fixed model and test, function-style contract, independent profile-likelihood oracle
difficulty_hypothesis: Agents drop incomplete participants and run a classical repeated-measures ANOVA, compare REML fits with different fixed effects, ignore the clustering, reach for lme4 (not installed) instead of the installed nlme, or fit time as a numeric trend and get the wrong degrees of freedom.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The standard answer in the wild uses lme4::lmer, which is not installed. Choosing nlme::lme and its ML/REML and VarCorr conventions is an API-availability and documentation question that package metadata and function documentation can inform (check_package_version, get_function_docs). It is not decisive: the lockfile and library(nlme) are available locally.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Which mixed-model package is installed and how nlme::lme exposes ML log-likelihoods, variance components and method = 'ML'.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes, partly: renv.lock and library(nlme) show availability, and nlme help is installed; MCP mainly shortens the lookup
alternative_solution_paths: nlme::lme with method = 'ML' for both models
nlme::gls with corCompSymm (equivalent for non-negative intraclass correlation)
an explicit profile-likelihood implementation in base R

calibration_risks.ceiling: low-moderate: needs the right package and the ML-versus-REML distinction
calibration_risks.floor: moderate: the optimiser-level tolerance is 1e-4 and the output contract is long

pinned_evidence.oracle: explicit profile-likelihood random-intercept ML (no nlme); cross-checked at load against nlme::lme logLik and sigma
